facts: Mobium has no driver for Wear OS of its own: the built-in backends are UiAutomator2 and uiautomator for Android, and WebDriverAgent for iOS simulators, iPhones and the Apple TV simulator.
A platform Mobium does not drive itself is reached through a driver: an executable named mobium-driver-<name> on the PATH, in any language, speaking JSON-RPC on stdio.

A driver needs snapshot, screenshot and tap to be useful, and inherits locators, refs, waiting, scrolling, the CLI, MCP and all five clients; examples/drivers/ has the guide and a reference driver in Python.
note: Following q058's pattern, kind fact, gold README.md#drivers-for-other-platforms — but Wear OS is Android: adb and UiAutomator2 run there, so the Android backend may simply work, unmeasured, and the honest answer may be 'untested' rather than 'write a driver'. Nothing in the docs says either. The stored answer (MobiumTV's UIKit screens) is a hallucination from an unrelated ROADMAP passage.
ask: Wear OS: answer 'untested — it is Android, the Android backend may work' (needs a doc line first), or the Tizen ruling (no driver, anyone can write one)? Worth measuring on a Wear OS emulator?
